# Synthetic study records

## N1: Pilot contrast
Six independent runs. Treatment minus baseline mean: +0.2 percentage points. Reported 95% confidence interval: [-4.0, +4.4] percentage points. Two-sided p = 0.91. The planning document sets ±1 percentage point as the smallest practically meaningful difference. No protocol deviations are recorded.

## N2: Confirmatory equivalence contrast
Independent randomized runs under the specified benchmark protocol. Before collecting data, the protocol set equivalence bounds at [-1, +1] percentage point and specified two one-sided tests at alpha = 0.05. The estimated contrast is +0.1 percentage point; its reported 90% confidence interval is [-0.3, +0.5]. Both one-sided tests reject their respective null at the prespecified alpha. Protocol and uncertainty assumptions were checked in the supplied audit. The data concern this benchmark and configuration only.

## C1: Observational adjustment
Dataset A contains 40 existing systems evaluated by their original authors. Algorithm family X averages 5 points above Y before adjustment. A regression adding model size and training-data volume estimates an X–Y contrast of 0.1 points, with 95% interval [-1.4, +1.6]. Assignment to X or Y was not randomized; data quality, tuning effort, and measurement error were not assessed. A draft says: "Controlling size made the gap disappear, proving size causes the entire advantage."

## C2: Randomized intervention
A preregistered experiment independently randomized 400 eligible instances to intervention A or B. The prespecified estimand is the average effect of assignment on task completion within this population and protocol. Difference A–B: +4.0 percentage points, reported 95% interval [+2.0, +6.0]. The supplied audit records no missing outcomes, noncompliance, interference, protocol changes, or differential measurement. The investigators make no mechanistic or new-population claim.

## M1: Benchmark draft
Our system increased exact-match accuracy from 71% to 75% on a fixed set of 200 short English arithmetic items. The draft concludes: "This establishes improved general reasoning ability across languages and real-world decisions." No additional tasks, languages, measures, or construct-validation evidence are supplied.

## M2: Bounded benchmark draft
Research question: Does a fixed parsing change improve exact-match accuracy on this specified, frozen English arithmetic item set under a fixed decoding budget? Primary measure: exact-match accuracy on that set. Controls: same checkpoint, same inputs and decoding budget; no item-level tuning. The proposal explicitly restricts its conclusion to this benchmark and budget and proposes paired item-level uncertainty analysis. It does not claim general reasoning ability or transfer.

## U1: Researcher's note
My proposal concerns whether plain-language wording reduces navigation mistakes with sign location held fixed. I have not yet explained the study to you. The draft contains fluent text on cognitive load, construct validity, and a controlled comparison. No demonstration of my own understanding is supplied.

## D1: Resource note
Three weeks, six person-hours per week, printing budget 30 dollars. Room access, recruitment, and required institutional review are pending. No participant consent has been collected. Publicly reusable floor-plan files are available, and a paper prototype can be inspected by its designer without participants. There are no existing task-completion observations. The desired claim concerns wording and navigation mistakes.
